backend_enablers.what_plain: The backend connects to the gas detector vendor's cloud, pulls device and reading data on a fixed cycle (every 45 seconds; the detectors themselves upload about every 30 minutes), removes duplicates, and raises alerts when a reading passes its alarm point. It also accepts the vendor's push messages and keeps a record of each one.
backend_enablers.note: Vendor cloud ("black box") path. Poll cadence and upload cadence are from commit 7a13cbb text. Push receiver was made deliberately unauthenticated in a3570a4 (internal note only).

backend_enablers.what_plain: New read endpoints serve the gas screens: detectors (with a stale flag and reading age), a summary with live and acknowledged alert counts, alerts, zones and alarm thresholds.
People with edit access can acknowledge and close a gas alert, recorded with who and when. Nothing is written back to the vendor.
backend_enablers.note: Two POST routes. If this build is not deployed, the Alerts buttons fail with "This could not be recorded". Deploy state unverified.

backend_enablers.what_plain: A full lightning module: ingests sensor packets, tracks each device state, marks a device stale after missing heartbeats, serves state and history to the portal, and registers devices automatically from the node registry.
backend_enablers.note: Staleness is 4 missed heartbeats on master since 22 Sep (was 3).

backend_enablers.what_plain: Alerting radii are stored as structured numbers (red radius, yellow radius, all-clear delay) and an administrator can store a sensor location for the map.

Lightning state changes to red, fault or offline are raised as observations to the platform Observation Manager and stored with delivery status; the lightning email and SMS notification engine was removed in favour of that.
backend_enablers.note: Delivery behaviour in production unverified: observation dispatch was disabled by hotfix 5869f6d (404 storm), then made unconditional in 0349c35 (30 Sep).

backend_enablers.what_plain: The whole safety policy publishes as one all-or-nothing action with a server-side check on changes that loosen it; a new "policy impact" calculation tells the screen how many of the last 30 days a limit would have stopped work.

Every safety-configuration change is version-checked and audited with before and after values, an actor name that resolves to a person, a coverage check and a compliance export; a change-proposal route creates pending requests that a second person approves.
Stations can have a display name; a Maximum Values report endpoint computes max heat index and wind speed per reading and per day; the old historical-data endpoint was removed.
The backend records which products a project has switched on; the portal reads it to decide which products to show. A project with no record shows none.

The backend now speaks MCP (the protocol AI agents use) as a second door beside the REST API. 33 tools: readings, thresholds, station health, agent summary, audit history, dashboard layout and a card catalogue, plus tools that only propose changes. Proposals need a second person to approve; the agent cannot approve its own.
backend_enablers.direction: DIRECTION / not live today: this is the plumbing that lets a future AI agent be fed everything about the site environment. No agent is switched on for customers; the FE composition features are default OFF.
backend_enablers.note: 33 = entries in McpToolSurfaceTests ExpectedToolNames at origin/master (4 Oct). The tool list covers weather and observer/agent-observation tools; there is no gas or lightning MCP tool in that list.

backend_enablers.what_plain: The safety summary now carries an advisory work decision (safe to work, controlled work, stop work, unknown) that cannot contradict the verdict, and a dashboard-composition contract (promoted cards, dynamic chart plan) that is additive.
An "observer" control plane stores findings an agent drafts in its own tables, with human-only review.

Devices reach the platform on several paths: Modbus devices on the wireless mesh (weather station, solar charge controller, lightning sensor) are told apart by a device tag and an unknown type is skipped without blocking others; the lightning sensor also has its own queue; gas detectors come through the vendor cloud, not Modbus.
